code.originalText: Twelve-week review: back and thumb on home programs, weight, blood pressure, mood, anxiety and sleep, and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Twelve-week review: back, thumb, weight, blood pressure, mood, anxiety and sleep. [S]

Mr. Marciano returns twelve weeks after intake. He finished the omeprazole a week ago and has had no stomach symptoms since. His back pain averages about 2 out of 10 on his morning exercises, and he now jogs three miles three times a week and swims twice a week without leg pain. The thumb splint is only needed for heavy gripping, and the thumb aches about 2 out of 10. His home blood pressure readings last week averaged 118/74 mmHg. He has lost 3.8 kg since intake. He sleeps seven to eight hours and wakes rested. He feels settled in retirement and says he is not worried or tense. He has no headaches, memory trouble, irritability or balance problems. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 122/76 mmHg, pulse 58; weight 88.2 kg
Normal strength, reflexes and sensation in the legs; normal gait and tandem walk
Minimal tenderness at the base of the thumb; pinch painless
Chronic mechanical low back pain for about seven years of heavy training and fighting, aching across the lower back, worse after long drives and in the morning
S — Synthetic chronic back pain anchored to his documented back injuries during his career.

Lumbar disc herniation at L4-L5 with left L5 radiculopathy, a few weeks old and improving: sharp pain into the left buttock and calf after bending to lift a child at home, seen in a hospital emergency department, where MRI showed a left paracentral L4-L5 disc extrusion contacting the left L5 nerve root; leg pain now intermittent, with slight numbness over the top of the left foot and normal strength; no bladder or bowel change
S — Synthetic modern presenting problem anchored to his documented ruptured disc; the level, side and MRI findings are synthetic.

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis of the left thumb base (first carpometacarpal joint) after an old fracture at the base of the first metacarpal from his early fighting years, with pain on pinching and gripping, an ache after long gripping, and a positive grind test
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented broken hands; which bones he broke is not recorded, and the left thumb is a synthetic choice.
Overweight after retirement, with a weight gain of about 9 kg in the four months since he stopped training, eating as he did in training camp; BMI 28.7
S — Synthetic weight change anchored to his documented heavy training and its sudden end at retirement.
Elevated blood pressure reading at intake (136/86 mmHg, average of two) without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings to confirm
S — Synthetic finding after the end of heavy training; resolved with weight loss and exercise.

History of repetitive head impacts from about thirteen years of Army, amateur and professional boxing, including heavy sparring; no remembered loss of consciousness; normal brain health baseline (no cognitive, mood or behavioral complaints; MoCA 29); traumatic encephalopathy syndrome not suspected
S — Synthetic risk-factor problem anchored to his documented career and sparring; no concussion or brain injury is documented in the sources read.

Epigastric pain and burning for six days after about seven weeks of near-daily naproxen, worse at night and on an empty stomach; no vomiting, black stools, blood or weight loss; normal hemoglobin; no alarm features; NSAID-associated dyspepsia
S — Synthetic acute problem from the oral NSAID; not a historical claim.
